overall_reason: The retention cohort table in the hero is a genuinely good product picture, but it sits on a stock SaaS skeleton (product-mock hero, fake logo strip, three feature rows, unsourced stat band, three pricing tiers, 'Ready to get started?' band, link-farm footer) with rival-swap-proof copy at every heading; the de-carded feature rows and navy-on-grey palette swap one default for another.

findings.where: whole page, section order (image.png top to bottom)
findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER: product-mock hero, logo strip ("Trusted by fast-moving teams at"), three feature rows, four-figure stat band, three pricing tiers with a highlighted middle, CTA band, four-column footer with newsletter: 7 stock sections in stock order.
findings.before: Hero > logos > 3 features > stat band > 3 tiers > CTA band > footer
findings.after: Build the page around the cohort table: walk one real question ("why did the Aug 4 cohort hold better?") through the product, and cut logos, stat band and CTA band unless real data exists
findings.why: Seven stock sections in order reads as a default page however specific the hero visual is.

findings.where: logo strip under hero; Team workspaces row
findings.evidence: Customer names "Northwind", "Lumen", "Vertex", "Quanta", "Beacon", "Atlas" are the default fake-brand set (Northwind is Microsoft's sample-database company), set as plain bold text; "Maya annotated Tuesday" uses a default-cast first name.
findings.before: Trusted by fast-moving teams at Northwind / Lumen / Vertex / Quanta / Beacon / Atlas
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real customer logos with permission] or remove the strip
findings.why: Invented customer names presented as social proof are fabricated proof.

findings.evidence: "12,000+ Teams onboard", "8B Events / month", "4.9 Average rating", "99.99% Uptime SLA": four round, unsourced figures over one-word labels; "4.9 Average rating" names no platform; the CTA repeats "Join thousands of teams".
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: sourced figures with as-of date and rating source] or delete the band
findings.why: An unsourced stat strip is invented proof; the hero already shows better evidence (the cohort table).

findings.where: h1, hero sub-line, section heads, CTA band
findings.evidence: T-FRESH-READER lines that fit any SaaS site: "Product analytics that just works" (h1), "Seamlessly powerful, beautifully simple.", "Everything you need to understand your users", "Simple, transparent pricing", "Ready to get started?". T-RIVAL-NAME: replace Cadence with Amplitude or Mixpanel and every head stays true.
findings.after: A head built from what the hero visual shows, e.g. "See which signup week stuck, without writing SQL" (only if Cadence can back it)
findings.why: Heads and hero are the most-read lines; all of them are stock phrases, including the 'seamlessly' slop word.

findings.where: features section and every section top
findings.evidence: Failed T-OVER-CORRECTION: the card grid has become three hairline rows each ending in a tiny decorative chart (sparkline "events in the last hour", three bars "visit, sign up, invite") with no axes or values; every section opens with the same 2px navy rule under a bold head (features, pricing, footer). T-DELETION: removing the mini charts loses nothing.
findings.before: Head + 2px rule + three equal rows each with a micro-viz
findings.after: Give one feature the room the cohort table has (a real funnel with numbers) and let the other two be a sentence each; vary the section openers
findings.why: The substitute habit (rules and micro-viz instead of cards) multiplies across the page and is itself a recognisable default.

findings.evidence: "No SQL required", "5 min to first chart", "SOC 2 compliant" set as a three-up mini stat row; "5 min" and "SOC 2" are unsourced claims presented as figures.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: SOC 2 report type and date; measured time-to-first-chart] or fold the true ones into the sub-line
findings.why: Bare figures as badges read as invented specifics unless the page backs them.

strengths: The hero 'Weekly retention by signup week' cohort table is a real, legible product picture: plausible decaying percentages, a labelled legend (Fewer ... More still active), and printed values in every cell. Keep it and build around it.
Restrained palette (navy, one blue ramp, cool grey) with no gradients, glows or icon tiles; pricing tiers list concrete limits.
not_investigated: Image-only item: no DOM, fonts, or mechanical sweep; look-family tells judged by eye only.
No 00-contract.md: brand palette and copy ownership unknown.
